description:
From the fz-kdt.127 cold review (2026-09-02, F7; prototype (A) measured
over 466 fixtures: 55 canon movers, 0 behaviour movers). Keeping capture
types in the forwarder key splits not only same-lambda/different-type
literals (the 127 shape) but ANY forwarder that receives closures with
different capture tuples from DIFFERENT lambdas: spawn/1 -> closure[?](pid)
vs closure[?](pid, int) (actor_ring 22->24 executables); enum_take_drop_
split 196->204 and 0->2 dispatch nodes (real atom+identity questions in
the recursive core); mailbox_closure_each 29->31; mailbox_closure_reduce
39->41; enum_predicate_search 204->206; enum_map_family 151->152; 00275
25->26; 00277 180->181; a_mixed 28->29; repr_seam 21->22. R3's "3 splits"
undercounted (it counted same-lambda slots only). Proportional-compilation
follow-up to fz-kdt.127 stage (A): is capture ARITY/shape (not type) the
right forwarder grain for different-lambda slots, or should the erasure
keep types only where a downstream consumer is specialized on them?
Measure against the inventory pins (204->206 re-pinned with cause).
title: Type-preserving forwarder keys split forwarders by capture TUPLE across different lambdas (spawn/1: closure[?](pid) vs (pid,int)): 55 canon movers, 11 fixtures gain executables
